captive_summary: This is the Iran LNG project at Tombak (owner match: IGEC 49% / Oil Industry Investment Co ~50% / Oil Industry Pension Fund 1%, matching GEM's listed owners almost exactly). The project's own design package included a dedicated on-site 1,130 MW CCGT power station (5 gas + 2 steam turbines) purpose-built to power the LNG plant, engineered/constructed by MAPNA-group companies from 2007. Because the LNG trains themselves have never started up (project suspended by the client since mid-2013 under sanctions), the completed power-plant units have instead been connected to Iran's national grid unit-by-unit since ~2022 to help meet national demand — but the plant was designed, sited, and built as this project's captive power block, which is a documented YES on design per SOP (as-designed captive power counts; partial/full grid export does not defeat a purpose-built captive finding).
confirmed_how: OGJ ('Iran details LNG liquefaction plans'): NIOC's Iran LNG project package breakdown includes Package I ('processing and condensation units, utility, offsite equipment...') and states 'Six gas turbine electrical drivers will supply the plant's power.' power-technology.com power-plant-profile page independently profiles the 'Iran LNG Combined Cycle Power Plant:' 1,130 MW, 5x162 MW + 2x160 MW turbines, Bushehr, 100%-owned by Iran LNG Co. MAPNA Group's own project page (mapnagroup.com/1232) confirms: 'Iran LNG Combined Cycle Power Plant... five gas and two steam units with a total capacity of 1130 Megawatts,' built for the Iran LNG program via Nirpars from 2007, with its fifth gas unit connected to the national grid July 2022. A separate MAPNA release (mapnagroup.com/31279) confirms four dedicated 3.3 MVA diesel gensets were also installed 'to provide backup power to the LNG site in case of emergencies' — diesel, so not itself a captive-gas source, but corroborates the site's ongoing dedicated electrical infrastructure.
